title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
description:
Each entry in triplets is a three-number array. You may repeatedly choose two entries and replace one of them with their coordinate-wise maximum. The other entry remains available. Return whether some entry can become exactly target after any number of these merges (including zero).

A coordinate larger than the corresponding target coordinate can never be reduced, so such an entry cannot contribute to the target.

Example 1

Input: triplets = [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]], target = [2,7,5]
Output: true

Explanation: Merging [2,5,3] and [1,7,5] produces [2,7,5]; the oversized middle entry is ignored.

Example 2

Input: triplets = [[3,4,5],[4,5,6]], target = [3,5,5]
Output: false

Explanation: One entry exceeds the last target coordinate, and the other exceeds the first.

Example 3

Input: triplets = [[1,1,1]], target = [1,1,1]
Output: true

Explanation: The existing entry already equals the target.

Constraints

  • 0 ≤ triplets.length ≤ 10,000.
  • Every entry of triplets and target contains exactly three integers.
  • 1 ≤ every coordinate ≤ 1,000.
